R_bidir.definition: Residue relation as operand: the structured trace-relation among residue conditions produced by lawful continuation.
R_bidir.not: Not itself the closure operator and not a direct causal updater.

closure_R.definition: Residue-conditioned closure: a relation between operands that is true while supported by admissible residue-conditioned topology.

formal_chain.closure_support: A ↔_R B is true iff closure support remains admissible under A_adm

allowed_operands: projection signatures only when explicitly marked _app
forbidden_operands: projection-only observables treated as process identity

decoupling_rules.definition: Decoupling occurs when residue-conditioned support no longer preserves admissible closure between operands.
conditions: nonzero distinction between operands is lost
closure topology cannot be preserved under allowed deformation
decoupling_rules.important_note: Decoupling is not automatically zero-state. It may be a local exclusion or boundary-generation event.

zero_state_condition.definition: Zero-state is total collapse of process participation caused by failure of the primary RT/Core closure.

vertical_bar_operator.name: Grouped closure participation
vertical_bar_operator.definition: Within TC_asym, the vertical bar marks grouped co-participation inside one closure expression, not logical OR, division, or separable alternatives.
vertical_bar_operator.reading: N2 and N3 participate as a grouped closure-side under residue-conditioned support.

reorientation_trigger.definition: Arb_A escalates to orientation-selection when current admissible continuation cannot preserve closure support under the existing orientation pattern.
reorientation_trigger.formal_candidate: Trigger_Reorient iff Q_current = ∅ OR closure support drops below its admissible threshold OR admissible deformation requires new -(i)

S_arbitration_rule.definition: The S-stage inside δ_a prunes candidate continuations that violate nonzero distinction, operand typing, residue compatibility, or closure support.

meta_relation_schema.definition: Family-level placeholder for legal typed binary relation operators.
meta_relation_schema.constraint: It is not a proof operator and does not grant truth by itself.
meta_relation_schema.legal_use: A <*>_x B requires x to specify admissibility, typing, and truth conditions.

truth_conditions: D(A|B) > ε or typed nonzero distinction is preserved
A and B remain coupled under context X
A and B do not collapse into the same operational role

blocked_items.reason: These depend on stabilized residue, closure, operand, and decoupling definitions.

governance_note.endorsement: formal patch only; not simulation evidence
governance_note.promotion_block: No downstream theorem or physics projection may promote from this patch alone.
